_doc: Registry of EXTERNAL third-party indices cited as CONTEXT ONLY. Never inputs to any Council of AI signed attestation. See context/README.md for the firewall doctrine. Every market-size figure is flagged is_projection:true. Every entry MUST carry a citation_note or context/firewall.py fails.
firewall: contextual — not part of the signed attestation

indices.name: Anthropic Economic Index (AEI)
indices.what_it_measures: How AI use maps onto real-world tasks and occupations, derived from anonymized Claude.ai conversations mapped to O*NET tasks and BLS occupational categories.
indices.citation_note: Launched 2025-02-10; underlying dataset open-sourced by Anthropic; task mapping uses U.S. DoL O*NET and BLS occupational taxonomies. Contextual signal only.

indices.name: ILO Working Paper 140 — Generative AI and Jobs
indices.what_it_measures: Global exposure of occupations/tasks to generative AI (augmentation vs. automation potential), by gender and income group.
indices.citation_note: doi:10.54394/HETP0387, published 2025-05-20. Reported finding: roughly 1 in 4 workers have some GenAI exposure and about 3.3% fall in the highest-exposure category. Exposure estimate, not an employment forecast. Contextual signal only.

indices.name: WEF Future of Jobs Report 2025
indices.what_it_measures: Employer-surveyed expectations of labour-market disruption, job creation and displacement, and skill shifts to 2030.
indices.citation_note: Published 2025-01-08. Projection: ~22% of jobs disrupted by 2030, with roughly +78M net new jobs (170M created, 92M displaced). Employer-survey projection, not a measured outcome. Contextual signal only.

indices.name: OECD AI Exposure Measure / AI Capability Gap Index
indices.what_it_measures: Occupational exposure to AI capabilities and the gap between current AI capability and the abilities occupations require.
indices.citation_note: OECD Artificial Intelligence Papers No. 59 (2026). Exposure/capability-gap measure; verify exact figures against the published paper before quoting. Contextual signal only.

indices.name: Stanford HAI AI Index 2026
indices.what_it_measures: Annual cross-cutting compendium of AI metrics: technical performance, economy, investment, policy, education, and responsible-AI indicators.
indices.citation_note: Stanford HAI AI Index Report 2026 edition. Aggregates third-party sources; treat each cited figure by its own provenance. Contextual signal only.

indices.name: Goldman Sachs — Humanoid robot: The AI accelerant
indices.what_it_measures: Projected total addressable market (TAM) for humanoid robots.
indices.citation_note: Published February 2024. PROJECTION: base-case TAM ~$38B by 2035, bull-case ~$154B by 2035. Scenario estimate, not a measurement. Contextual signal only.

indices.name: Morgan Stanley — Humanoid robots: The $5 Trillion Global Market
indices.what_it_measures: Projected long-run global market size for humanoid robots.
indices.citation_note: Published 2025-04-29. PROJECTION: ~$5T global market by 2050. Long-horizon scenario estimate, not a measurement. Contextual signal only.

indices.name: Humanity's Last Exam (HLE)
indices.publisher: Center for AI Safety (CAIS) & Scale AI
indices.what_it_measures: Frontier expert-level academic benchmark across many domains; provides a human-expert baseline against which model performance is compared.
indices.citation_note: Human-expert baseline reported around ~90%. Note: independent review found an error rate on the order of ~30% on portions of the question set, so the human baseline is contested; cite with that caveat. Contextual signal only.

indices.name: GPQA-Diamond
indices.what_it_measures: Graduate-level, Google-proof expert QA in biology, physics, and chemistry; the Diamond subset is the hardest, highest-agreement slice.
indices.citation_note: arXiv:2311.12022. Human baselines: domain experts ~65-74%; skilled non-experts ~34% even with web access. Baseline measurement from the paper. Contextual signal only.
